tabs.label: 1 · import
tabs.title: 1 · import: from spreadsheet to a locked file

blocks.text: **What it does.** It reads the spreadsheet staff have filled in, checks every row, and writes the rows to `batch1.jsonl` with a seal beside it.
**Why it exists.** The spreadsheet is filled in by hand. Import refuses the whole file when it finds a single problem, so only clean rows reach training.
One `.xlsx` workbook. Each tab is a case type. Row 1 is the header: `id`, `text`, one column per topic, then `none`.
`real/batch1.jsonl`: one line per comment. `real/batch1.sha256`: its seal.

items.text: Open the workbook as a zip file of XML, with Python's standard library.
Skip the tabs `exempel`, `hjälp` and `kategorier`. Every other tab is a case type.
If anything is wrong, list every problem by tab, row and column, and write nothing.

blocks.text: A name can be used once: a sealed file is never overwritten.

**What it does.** It pools the imported batches and cuts them into two sealed files.
